title: Internal Control Frameworks - COSO
exam_relevance: CRITICAL - Heavily tested on CPA AUD exam. Expect 5-8 questions on COSO framework, the 5 components, 17 principles, and application to audits. COSO is the most widely used internal control framework and is fundamental to understanding control effectiveness.
learning_objectives: Understand the COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework and its purpose
Master the 5 components of internal control and their interrelationships
Know all 17 principles associated with the 5 components
Understand how the framework applies to financial reporting controls
Differentiate between entity-level controls and activity-level controls
Understand control objectives, control activities, and control deficiencies
Apply COSO framework to audit planning and control testing
Understand COSO ERM (Enterprise Risk Management) framework basics

introduction.overview: The COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework is the most widely used framework for designing, implementing, and evaluating internal control systems. COSO (Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission) issued the original framework in 1992 and updated it in 2013.
introduction.what_is_coso: COSO is a joint initiative of five professional accounting organizations created to study factors leading to fraudulent financial reporting and make recommendations. The framework they developed has become the standard for internal control.
why_coso_matters: Required framework for SOX 404 compliance (management assessment of internal control over financial reporting for public companies)
Most widely accepted internal control framework in United States and globally
Provides common language for discussing internal control
Basis for auditor's understanding and evaluation of internal control
Framework for management to design and implement controls

key_versions.original_1992: Original COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework
key_versions.updated_2013: COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013) - current version with 17 principles
key_versions.coso_erm_2017: COSO Enterprise Risk Management Framework (2017) - broader framework including risk management

introduction.exam_importance: The CPA exam heavily tests the 5 components and 17 principles of COSO. You must memorize these and understand how they relate to financial reporting controls and audits.

definition_of_internal_control.coso_definition: Internal control is a process, effected by an entity's board of directors, management, and other personnel, designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the achievement of objectives in the following categories:

three_categories_of_objectives.operations: Effectiveness and efficiency of operations (operational objectives)
three_categories_of_objectives.reporting: Reliability of financial reporting (reporting objectives) - MOST important for auditors
three_categories_of_objectives.compliance: Compliance with applicable laws and regulations (compliance objectives)

key_characteristics.process: Internal control is a PROCESS - ongoing actions and activities, not a single event
key_characteristics.effected_by_people: Controls are performed by PEOPLE - board, management, employees at all levels
key_characteristics.reasonable_assurance: Controls provide REASONABLE assurance, not ABSOLUTE assurance. Controls have inherent limitations (human error, collusion, management override).
key_characteristics.objectives: Controls are designed to achieve specific objectives - must define objectives before can design controls

definition_of_internal_control.exam_emphasis: Internal control provides REASONABLE assurance (not absolute). It's a PROCESS involving people. These concepts are frequently tested.

five_components_of_internal_control.description: The COSO framework identifies 5 components of internal control. ALL FIVE components must be present and functioning effectively for internal control to be effective.
five_components_of_internal_control.mnemonic: CRIME: Control Environment, Risk Assessment, Information & Communication, Monitoring, (and Control) Activities (note: order differs slightly but helps remember all 5)

component_1_control_environment.description: The control environment is the SET OF STANDARDS, PROCESSES, AND STRUCTURES that provide the foundation for carrying out internal control across the organization. It's the 'tone at the top' - the overall attitude of management and board toward control.
component_1_control_environment.why_foundation: The control environment is the FOUNDATION for all other components. Even if other components are well-designed, weak control environment undermines effectiveness.
elements_of_control_environment: Board of directors independence and oversight
Commitment to competence (knowledge and skills needed)

strong_control_environment: Code of conduct communicated and enforced
Active, independent board and audit committee
Clear organizational structure with defined responsibilities
Hiring qualified people and providing training
weak_control_environment: Board not independent or not engaged
Pressure to meet targets at any cost

component_1_control_environment.exam_importance: Control environment is the FOUNDATION. Questions may describe company culture and ask whether control environment is strong or weak. Look for 'tone at the top,' management integrity, board oversight.

component_2_risk_assessment.description: Risk assessment is the process of identifying and analyzing RISKS to achieving objectives, forming a basis for determining how risks should be managed.
steps_in_risk_assessment: 1. Specify objectives clearly (what are we trying to achieve?)
2. Identify risks to achieving objectives (what could go wrong?)
3. Assess significance of identified risks (how material is the risk?)
4. Assess likelihood of identified risks occurring (how probable?)
5. Determine how to respond to risks (accept, avoid, reduce, share)

types_of_risks.external_risks: Economic changes, regulatory changes, natural disasters, competition
types_of_risks.internal_risks: Complexity of activities, employee turnover, system breakdowns, fraud

component_2_risk_assessment.change_considerations: Risk assessment must consider risks from external and internal CHANGES:
component_2_risk_assessment.fraud_risk: Risk assessment must specifically consider risk of FRAUD, including fraudulent financial reporting and misappropriation of assets.
component_2_risk_assessment.exam_emphasis: Risk assessment involves identifying risks AND determining how to respond. Changes in organization require updated risk assessment. Fraud risk must be considered.

component_3_control_activities.description: Control activities are the ACTIONS established through policies and procedures that help ensure management directives to mitigate risks are carried out.

segregation_of_duties.description: Different people should perform authorization, recordkeeping, and custody functions
segregation_of_duties.purpose: Reduces risk of error or fraud by requiring collusion for fraudulent activity
examples: Person who approves purchases should not also process payments
Person who receives cash should not also record cash receipts
Person who has custody of assets should not also maintain accounting records for those assets
segregation_of_duties.limitation: Small companies may not have enough personnel for adequate segregation - must use compensating controls

authorization_and_approval.description: Transactions and activities should be authorized by appropriate personnel
authorization_and_approval.general_authorization: Standing policy for routine transactions (e.g., all purchases under $5,000 approved by department manager)
authorization_and_approval.specific_authorization: Individual approval for non-routine transactions (e.g., board approval for acquisition)
authorization_and_approval.examples: Credit approval before sale, purchase order approval before purchase, budget approval before expenditure

physical_controls.description: Physical security over assets and records
examples: Locked storage for inventory and equipment
Access controls to IT systems and data centers

reconciliations.description: Comparison of two sets of records to ensure consistency
examples: Subsidiary ledger reconciliations to general ledger
Physical inventory counts to perpetual records
Accounts receivable aging to general ledger
reconciliations.key_point: Reconciliations must be REVIEWED and APPROVED by someone independent of the reconciler

performance_reviews.description: Review of actual performance against budgets, forecasts, and prior periods
examples: Comparison of financial metrics across locations

information_processing_controls.description: Controls over accuracy, completeness, and authorization of transactions
information_processing_controls.application_controls: Controls within specific applications (edit checks, validation, sequential numbering, exception reports)
information_processing_controls.general_it_controls: Overarching IT controls (access controls, change management, backups) - support application controls
examples: Edit checks on data entry (valid ranges, required fields)

component_3_control_activities.exam_strategy: Know the categories of control activities. Questions may describe a control and ask which category it falls into. Segregation of duties is most heavily tested.

component_4_information_and_communicatio.description: Information and communication are the identification, capture, and exchange of information in a form and timeframe that enable people to carry out their responsibilities.

information.requirement: Organization must obtain and use RELEVANT, QUALITY information to support functioning of internal control
information.sources: Internal sources (operational data, financial data) and external sources (market data, regulatory updates)
information.quality: Information must be accurate, timely, complete, accessible, and provided in appropriate detail
information.purpose: Enable personnel to carry out their control responsibilities

communication.internal_communication: Information must flow DOWN (management to employees), UP (employees to management), and ACROSS (between departments/functions)
communication.external_communication: Two-way communication with external parties (customers, suppliers, regulators, shareholders)
examples: Policies and procedures communicated to employees
Whistleblower hotline for employees to report concerns

component_4_information_and_communicatio.exam_note: Information must be relevant, quality, timely. Communication must occur in all directions (up, down, across, and external).

component_5_monitoring_activities.description: Monitoring activities are ongoing evaluations, separate evaluations, or some combination of the two used to ascertain whether each of the 5 components of internal control is present and functioning.

ongoing_monitoring.description: Built-in to normal business processes - occurs in real time as part of operations
examples: Customer complaints about billing (may indicate control breakdown)

separate_evaluations.description: Periodic assessments of controls - conducted separately from normal operations
separate_evaluations.frequency: Frequency depends on risk assessment and effectiveness of ongoing monitoring. Higher risk areas require more frequent evaluation.

deficiency_evaluation_and_communication.requirement: Control deficiencies must be IDENTIFIED, EVALUATED, and COMMUNICATED to appropriate personnel
deficiency_evaluation_and_communication.serious_matters: Serious matters (significant deficiencies, material weaknesses) must be reported to SENIOR MANAGEMENT and BOARD
deficiency_evaluation_and_communication.exam_point: Control deficiencies must be communicated. Material weaknesses must be communicated to board/audit committee.

five_components_of_internal_control.interrelationship_of_components: All 5 components must be present and functioning for effective internal control. Components work together - weakness in one component affects others. For example, weak control environment undermines other components even if they're well-designed.

seventeen_principles.description: The 2013 COSO framework identifies 17 PRINCIPLES that support the 5 components. Each principle has points of focus that assist in design and evaluation.
seventeen_principles.exam_importance: The 17 principles are testable. You should know which principles go with which component. The most important principles are heavily tested.

control_environment_principles_1_5.principle_1: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values

control_activities_principles_10_12.principle_11: Selects and develops general controls over technology

most_heavily_tested_principles: Principle 10: Control activities (especially segregation of duties)
Principle 17: Communicates deficiencies to appropriate parties
seventeen_principles.memorization_tip: Know that there are 17 principles total. Know the 5 components and that each has associated principles (Control Environment has 5, Risk Assessment has 4, Control Activities has 3, Info & Comm has 3, Monitoring has 2).

entity_level_vs_activity_level_controls.description: Internal controls can be categorized as entity-level or activity-level controls.

entity_level_controls.definition: Controls that have a pervasive effect on the organization - operate at the company-wide level
examples: Tone at the top and control environment
entity_level_controls.importance: Entity-level controls can have pervasive impact. Weak entity-level controls can undermine activity-level controls.
entity_level_controls.audit_impact: Auditors test entity-level controls to understand overall control environment

activity_level_controls.definition: Controls that operate at the process, transaction, or application level
activity_level_controls.audit_impact: Auditors test activity-level controls for specific assertions and accounts

control_objectives.definition: What the control is designed to achieve (the purpose)
control_objectives.examples: Ensure all valid transactions are recorded (completeness). Ensure only valid transactions are recorded (occurrence). Ensure transactions are recorded accurately (accuracy).
control_objectives.link_to_assertions: Control objectives often align with financial statement assertions

control_activities.definition: The specific actions taken to achieve control objectives
control_activities.examples: Monthly bank reconciliation reviewed by manager. Three-way match performed by AP clerk before payment approved.

control_deficiencies.description: When control is not designed or operating effectively to prevent or detect misstatements

three_levels.control_deficiency: Control doesn't operate as designed, or design is inadequate - but not significant
three_levels.significant_deficiency: Deficiency or combination of deficiencies that is LESS SEVERE than material weakness but important enough to merit attention by those charged with governance
three_levels.material_weakness: Deficiency or combination of deficiencies such that there is REASONABLE POSSIBILITY that a material misstatement will NOT be prevented or detected on a timely basis

communication_requirements.significant_deficiencies: MUST communicate IN WRITING to those charged with governance (board/audit committee)
communication_requirements.material_weaknesses: MUST communicate IN WRITING to those charged with governance

control_deficiencies.exam_emphasis: Know the three levels and that significant deficiencies and material weaknesses must be communicated IN WRITING to those charged with governance.

sox_404_and_management_assessment.description: For public companies, Section 404 of Sarbanes-Oxley Act requires management to assess and report on internal control over financial reporting (ICFR).
management_responsibilities: Accept responsibility for effectiveness of ICFR
Present written assessment of effectiveness in annual report
auditor_responsibilities: Express opinion on whether ICFR is effective (integrated audit)
sox_404_and_management_assessment.exam_note: SOX 404 requires management to assess ICFR using a framework like COSO. Auditor audits both financial statements AND ICFR for public companies.

coso_erm_framework.description: COSO Enterprise Risk Management Framework is a broader framework that encompasses internal control and adds strategic and operational risk management.
coso_erm_framework.erm_components: COSO ERM (2017) has 5 components and 20 principles (different from Internal Control framework)
coso_erm_framework.relationship: Internal Control framework focuses on control. ERM framework takes broader view of risk management across the enterprise, including strategy.
coso_erm_framework.exam_relevance: Internal Control framework is much more heavily tested than ERM. Know that ERM exists and is broader, but focus study on Internal Control framework.

practice_problems.question:
For each scenario below, identify which component of COSO internal control is primarily involved:

Scenario A: The CEO regularly emphasizes ethical behavior and has terminated employees who violated the code of conduct.

Scenario B: Management identifies that rapid growth has created risk of inadequate segregation of duties in newer locations.

Scenario C: The accounts payable clerk performs a three-way match (purchase order, receiving report, vendor invoice) before processing payments.

Scenario D: Monthly financial reports are provided to department managers showing actual vs. budget variances.

Scenario E: The internal audit department conducts quarterly testing of key controls.

scenario_A.reasoning: The CEO's emphasis on ethics and enforcement of consequences demonstrates 'tone at the top' and integrity/ethical values, which are fundamental elements of the control environment. This is the foundation for other controls.
scenario_A.principle: Principle 1: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values. Principle 5: Enforces accountability.

scenario_B.reasoning: Management is IDENTIFYING a risk (inadequate segregation due to rapid growth) and analyzing how it affects control objectives. This is the risk assessment process - identifying and analyzing risks, particularly risks from changes (rapid growth).
scenario_B.principle: Principle 7: Identifies and analyzes risk. Principle 9: Identifies and analyzes significant changes.

scenario_C.reasoning: The three-way match is a specific CONTROL PROCEDURE performed to mitigate risk of paying for invalid or inaccurate purchases. This is a control activity - the specific action taken to achieve control objectives.
scenario_C.principle: Principle 10: Selects and develops control activities.
scenario_C.note: Control activities are the actual procedures performed (authorization, reconciliation, physical controls, etc.)

scenario_D.reasoning: Financial reports being provided to managers is COMMUNICATION of INFORMATION. Managers need this information to carry out their control responsibilities (monitoring budget, managing operations). The reports flow information to those who need it.
scenario_D.principle: Principle 13: Uses relevant information. Principle 14: Communicates internally.
scenario_D.note: Information must be relevant, timely, and communicated to appropriate personnel

scenario_E.reasoning: Internal audit testing is a SEPARATE EVALUATION of controls - conducted periodically to assess whether controls are present and functioning. This is monitoring (specifically, separate evaluation type of monitoring).
scenario_E.principle: Principle 16: Conducts ongoing and/or separate evaluations.
scenario_E.note: Internal audit testing, external audit testing, and management's SOX 404 assessment are all examples of separate evaluations (monitoring)

tip_1_memorize_five_components.description: The 5 components are fundamental - must know them cold
tip_1_memorize_five_components.five_components: 1. Control Environment, 2. Risk Assessment, 3. Control Activities, 4. Information & Communication, 5. Monitoring
tip_1_memorize_five_components.mnemonic: CRIME (Control env, Risk, Info/comm, Monitoring, (control) Activities) - order differs but helps remember all 5
tip_1_memorize_five_components.exam_question: Question may ask 'which component addresses...' or may describe situation and ask which component

tip_2_control_environment_foundation.key_point: Even if other components are well-designed, weak control environment undermines them
tip_2_control_environment_foundation.tone_at_top: Look for 'tone at the top,' management integrity, board oversight, ethical values
tip_2_control_environment_foundation.exam_scenario: Question describes management that overrides controls or pressures employees - this is weak control environment

tip_3_seventeen_principles.description: Know there are 17 principles and which component each relates to
tip_3_seventeen_principles.breakdown: Control Environment (5), Risk Assessment (4), Control Activities (3), Info & Comm (3), Monitoring (2)
tip_3_seventeen_principles.most_tested: Board oversight (Principle 2), Fraud risk (Principle 8), Control activities (Principle 10), Communicate deficiencies (Principle 17)
tip_3_seventeen_principles.exam_strategy: Don't need to memorize all 17 word-for-word, but know the key ones and the count by component

tip_4_reasonable_assurance.description: Internal control provides REASONABLE assurance, not ABSOLUTE
tip_4_reasonable_assurance.limitations: Human error, collusion, management override, cost-benefit considerations
tip_4_reasonable_assurance.exam_trap: Question may ask if control provides 'absolute assurance' or 'guarantee' - answer is NO (only reasonable assurance)

tip_5_deficiency_levels.description: Know the three levels of control deficiencies
tip_5_deficiency_levels.levels: Control deficiency < Significant deficiency < Material weakness
tip_5_deficiency_levels.communication: Significant deficiencies and material weaknesses must be communicated IN WRITING to those charged with governance
tip_5_deficiency_levels.exam_question: Question describes control problem and asks severity level or who to communicate to

tip_6_all_five_required.description: ALL 5 components must be present and functioning
tip_6_all_five_required.key_point: Can't compensate for missing component by strengthening others. All 5 required.
tip_6_all_five_required.exam_scenario: Question may ask if control is effective when one component is missing - answer is NO

tip_7_segregation_of_duties.description: Segregation of duties is most tested control activity
tip_7_segregation_of_duties.incompatible_functions: Same person should not: (1) authorize AND record, (2) have custody AND record, (3) authorize AND have custody
tip_7_segregation_of_duties.exam_question: Question describes person who does multiple incompatible functions - this violates segregation

tip_8_fraud_risk.description: Risk assessment must specifically address fraud risk
tip_8_fraud_risk.types: Fraudulent financial reporting and misappropriation of assets
tip_8_fraud_risk.exam_point: Risk assessment is not complete without considering fraud risk

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Describe scenario, ask which COSO component
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Look for keywords: ethics/tone (control environment), identifying risks (risk assessment), specific procedure (control activities), information flow (info & comm), evaluation/testing (monitoring)

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Which is NOT a component of internal control?
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Know the 5 components. Wrong answers often include: assurance, implementation, effectiveness, design

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: Describe control problem, ask severity level
common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Material misstatement possible = material weakness. Important but less severe = significant deficiency. Minor = control deficiency

common_exam_question_patterns.pattern: What provides foundation for internal control?

common_exam_question_patterns.approach: Identify if same person has incompatible duties: authorize/record/custody - should be separated

memorization_aids.five_components: CRIME: Control Environment, Risk Assessment, Information & Communication, Monitoring, (control) Activities
memorization_aids.seventeen_principles: 5-4-3-3-2 (5 for Control Env, 4 for Risk, 3 for Activities, 3 for Info/Comm, 2 for Monitoring)
memorization_aids.reasonable_assurance: IC = RA (Internal Control = Reasonable Assurance, not absolute)
memorization_aids.deficiency_levels: CD < SD < MW (Control Deficiency < Significant Deficiency < Material Weakness)

key_concepts: COSO framework has 5 components: Control Environment, Risk Assessment, Control Activities, Information & Communication, Monitoring
Control environment is the FOUNDATION - tone at the top, board oversight, integrity
ALL 5 components must be present and functioning for effective control
Internal control provides REASONABLE assurance (not absolute) due to inherent limitations
Control deficiency < Significant deficiency < Material weakness
Significant deficiencies and material weaknesses must be communicated IN WRITING to those charged with governance
Risk assessment must specifically address fraud risk
Segregation of duties is key control activity (separate authorization, recordkeeping, custody)
Information must be relevant and quality; communication must flow in all directions
critical_for_exam: Know all 5 components and be able to identify them in scenarios
17 principles total (know the count by component: 5-4-3-3-2)
All 5 components required - can't compensate for missing component
Three levels of deficiencies and communication requirements
Segregation of duties is most tested control activity
common_mistakes: Forgetting that control environment is the foundation
Thinking control provides absolute assurance (it's reasonable)
Not recognizing that all 5 components are required
Confusing the components (e.g., thinking specific procedure is risk assessment rather than control activity)
Not knowing that significant deficiencies must be communicated IN WRITING to governance
Forgetting that fraud risk must be specifically assessed

primary_standards: AU-C Section 315: Understanding the Entity and Its Environment and Assessing the Risks of Material Misstatement
PCAOB AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements

related_topics: internal_control_testing - testing the effectiveness of the 5 components and associated controls
fraud_risk_assessment - Principle 8 of COSO requires fraud risk assessment
audit_planning_procedures - understanding internal control is part of audit planning
audit_reports_opinions - material weaknesses affect auditor's opinion on ICFR
